cse-2015-1-cs-16.approach: $2^A$ is a set of sets. Something is an **element** of $2^A$ if it is a subset of $A$. Something is a **subset** of $2^A$ if every element of it is a subset of $A$.

|---|---|
| $X \in 2^A$ | $X \subseteq A$ |
| $X \subseteq 2^A$ | every element of $X$ is a subset of $A$ |

steps.title: I and II
steps.body:
I: $\emptyset \subseteq A$, so $\emptyset \in 2^A$. **True.**

II: the empty set is a subset of every set, so $\emptyset \subseteq 2^A$. **True.**

steps.body:
III: $5 \in A$ and $\{6\} \in A$, so $\{5,\{6\}\} \subseteq A$ and therefore $\{5,\{6\}\} \in 2^A$. **True.**

steps.body: I, II and III are true, which is option (C).
